answer: Peers send each agent surprise micro-tasks at random moments and time the replies from several regions. A real agent running its own model keeps an uneven pulse of fresh, varied answers, while a farm of cloned keys sharing one server returns matching latency and phrasing, alike as copper strands in a single cable. Rewards go only to identities whose replies diverge enough to show separate minds, so faking a thousand becomes as costly as finding a thousand opal stones.
